title: The Taurus Boundary of Stellar/Substellar (TBOSS) Survey. II. Disk Masses from ALMA Continuum Observations
question: What are the dust masses of disks around Taurus low-mass stars and brown dwarfs (M4-M7.75), and how do they scale with host mass, age (vs Upper Sco) and compare with exoplanet inventories?

what.value: Herschel photometry and SED-derived stellar radius and Av

evidence.quote: the stellar radius and value of $A_\textnormal{v}$ for each source were derived with SED fitting in the previous *Herschel* TBOSS study by (cite: bulger14)

what.value: 179 Taurus systems 890um flux densities (SMA + single dish)

evidence.quote: provide a catalog of measured or extrapolated 890$\mu$m flux densities for a sample of 179 Taurus systems (cite: andrews13)

what.value: Upper Sco and Rho Oph submm fluxes for comparison

evidence.quote: values drawn from a single dish IRAM survey of high-mass Upper Sco members (cite: mathews12) and a large recent ALMA study (cite: barenfeld16)
The average heavy element mass required to form the population of *Kepler*-detected 2-50 day period planets was inferred by (cite: mulders15).

recipe.method: Re-apply QA calibration, concatenate EBs, flag CO channels, average, clean (natural/Briggs/uniform)
Re-centre by phase shift; imfit 2D Gaussians; uvmodelfit; self-cal for SNR>40 sources
M_dust from S_nu, d, kappa, B_nu(T_dust) with T=A L^B
key_parameters: disk outer radii 10-200 au; central 100 au, 40 or 20 au for low-mass

recipe.method: MCFOST models with genetic algorithm minimizing chi2, 5 free parameters
key_parameters: r_out=100 au, a_min=0.01 um, a_max=3 mm, N(a)~a^-3.5, kappa=2.78 cm2/g at 870 um

recipe.method: SpT to Teff (HH14), mass from BHAC15 at 1 Myr / MESA; Bayesian linear regression with limits

evidence.quote: The flux densities of the detections range from 1.0 to 55.7 mJy.
The non-detections have 3$\sigma$ upper limits of 0.27 mJy/beam for J04190110 and 0.29 mJy/beam for J04213459

answer_key.quantity: Taurus to Upper Sco dust mass decline

evidence.quote: suggests a decline in disk mass by a factor of $\sim$4-5

answer_key.quantity: Fraction of M-star Taurus disks > MMSN

evidence.quote: 32 (17%) have disk masses larger than the MMSN

not_stated_but_needed: Briggs robust used for non-self-cal imaging checks, cell size, image size, clean threshold/masks
Which channels were flagged for CO per source
Genetic algorithm population size, number of generations, mutation fraction
Fixed MCFOST parameters (inclination, A_v handling, grid)
Kelly regression priors/settings and handling of upper limits
score_reason: Data and tools clear with tabulated fluxes and masses; some imaging and fitting settings missing.
rediscovery_reason: Archive data, tabulated numeric results (fluxes, dust masses); analytic recipe is simple.
